Fixed: ci/contract_review/service.py tracker_patterns() reads the patterns of no-tracker-text-shipped from the newest idiomatic-project spec, so the validator and the rule share one definition. Nothing left to enforce.

A tracker id of four letters and no digit is the same text as a product or crate short name of four letters, so a glob cannot tell them apart; the digit requirement in no-tracker-text-shipped is the deliberate trade. Tastemaker cannot prove what is a tracker id without the tracker's id list; the control is review. Decided none.

Measured: the four planted spellings in sdk lib.rs give 0 no-tracker-text-shipped findings. They carry no digit, so the same limit holds: the text is indistinguishable from a short product name. Widening the globs during the freeze would trade this miss for false positives on names; decided none, review is the control.

Measured: the planted short name in parentheses gives 1 no-tracker-text-shipped finding (a false positive). It is the mirror of the no-digit trade: a three-letter tracker id and a three-letter short name are the same text. The author rephrases or ignores in source with a reason; a new spec version during the freeze is not worth one wording. Decided none.
